title: Container with Most Water
kidExplanation: Vertical sticks in a row. Choose two sticks as walls; rainwater forms a rectangle. Maximize the water.
plainProblem: Container with Most Water: Vertical sticks in a row. Worked example — input: height = [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7]; expected output: 49. Why: Best area. Interview pattern to name out loud: Two pointers from both ends (or slow/fast).

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Container with Most Water”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input height = [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7] should still produce 49.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To find the maximum area of water that can be held between two vertical lines, we can use a two-pointer approach. We initialize two pointers, one at the beginning of the input array (left) and the other at the end of the array (right). The area between the two vertical lines is calculated as the minimum of the heights at the two pointers multiplied by the distance between them. We then update the maximum area found so far and move the pointer with the smaller height towards the other pointer. We continue this process until the two pointers meet or cross each other.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Commit to Two pointers from both ends (or slow/fast). Sorted array, palindrome, or pair-sum hints. Walk example `height = [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7]` → `49` while naming each variable, then code. Close with O(n) time and O(1) space.
